status: ESCALATION — the edit fixes W1-35 TestWording, but W2-11's own test needs the word `PYTHONPATH` in brief-lead.md, so the two acceptance tests can't both pass.

evidence: Commit 095167b8 "W2-11 r1 repair 3: brief-lead's code-under-test bullet names no language or runner; the setting stays a placeholder", with trailers Task: DAEO-k7hz / Implements: DEC-534, DEC-539, DEC-732, CAP-33 / Role: product-spec / Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>. 1 file changed, 1 insertion, 1 deletion. No pre-commit hook was present (checked before committing).
tests: TestWording (W1-35) plus test_w2_11_briefs.py: **62 passed, 1 failed** in 0.21s. The failure: `tests/acceptance/W2-11/test_w2_11_briefs.py::test_the_lead_brief_carries_the_role_independent_rule[the code under test per command]` — "AssertionError: brief-lead.md does not state the code under test per command (DEC-732)". The assertion has two parts: `s.cites(text, 'DEC-732')` is True, and `s.stated(text, ['PYTHONPATH'])` returns `[]`. W1-35 TestWording, including `test_tests_are_named_without_a_language_or_a_runner`, now passes.
discoveries: (1) The two acceptance tests contradict each other. W1-35 (DEC-534) forbids naming a language or runner in kernel text. The W2-11 briefs test requires the literal `PYTHONPATH` in brief-lead.md under DEC-732. The previous worker's parenthesis satisfied the W2-11 test and broke W1-35; removing it does the opposite. (2) The search found no other language or runner name in the five brief templates, `skill.md`, or the audit, change, checkpoint, discovery, orchestration, planning, qa-review, retrieval and test-design skills, including their extra files. (3) The only other matches are in the vendored `template/governance/kernel/skills/superpowers/` skills (test-driven-development: `jest.fn()`, `npm test`, "bare `pytest`, `npm test`, `cargo test`"; systematic-debugging: `npm test` in root-cause-tracing.md and find-polluter.sh). Those skills aren't among the changed ones, and their names are worked examples rather than the same kind of example, so I left them alone.
risks: Whichever way the line reads, one acceptance test stays red. The W2-11 test was written by an independent test designer. Changing the test, or putting a language name back in, needs a decision I can't make.
lessons: Before adding or removing a concrete name in kernel text, run W1-35 TestWording and the W2-11 briefs test together. Their requirements on brief-lead.md conflict.
proposed_decisions: PKG-1, the DEC-534 vs DEC-732 conflict in brief-lead.md (DEC-105, three options). (A) Apply now: the independent-test-designer changes the W2-11 briefs case to accept the placeholder `<the setting that selects the code under test>=<worktree path>/src` instead of the literal `PYTHONPATH`. That keeps kernel text free of language names (DEC-534, DEC-539) and is one test-designer pass, about 10 minutes. (B) Defer: record the case as a known red against W1-35 until round 2. Cheap, but the ticket can't close green. (C) Re-baseline: let the code-under-test rule name the setting per language as a stated exception to DEC-534. That changes a closed spec and touches the W1-35 test. I recommend (A), confidence 0.8: DEC-534 is the older rule and has a test guarding it, and the role-independent rule is meant to be language-neutral.
unresolved: The one W2-11 briefs case above is red. The owner or orchestrator needs to choose an option in PKG-1.
recommended_next_action: The ticket lead escalates PKG-1. If (A) is chosen, it sends the W2-11 briefs case back to the independent-test-designer to accept the placeholder form.
